subject: PrivateNet: Intermittent authentication failures observed after control-plane upgrade
messages:
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>
To: Sofia Martinez <sofiam@helixhealth.com>
Cc: Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwoodinference.com>, Dylan Brooks <dylan.brooks@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: PrivateNet: Intermittent authentication failures observed after control-plane upgrade

Hi Sofia,

I wanted to reach out immediately with a status update — we detected intermittent authentication failures affecting Helix Health's PrivateNet cluster starting at ~08:45 PDT following our control-plane rolling upgrade. You may have seen 502s and webhook delivery retries in the past 30 minutes.

What we know so far:
- Impact window: ~08:45–09:05 PDT (some spikes of failed RPCs outside this window observed)
- Symptom: token validation errors and short-lived 401/502 responses for management-plane calls and webhook delivery failures
- Scope: Helix Health private deployment (cluster id: hlx-prod-5), not the hosted API

Immediate actions taken:
- Our engineers triggered a targeted rollback of the most recent control-plane pod rotation in the affected region to reduce error volume (completed 09:01 PDT).
- We've captured control-plane logs and KV/auth-cache traces (attaching controlplane-logs-0625.tar.gz).
- A bridgecall is scheduled at 13:00 PDT today to walk through findings and next steps; I can move this if you need an earlier time.

Requested info that would help with triage:
- Any error IDs or internal correlation ids you saw (Helix logs or UIDs)
- Were there any operational changes on your side around 08:30–09:00 PDT (token rotation, proxy config, network ACLs)?

We're treating this as high priority and I'll keep you updated as we gather more evidence. Apologies for the disruption — we know this impacts your downstream workflows.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Tue, 25 Jun 2028 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Bridge notes and short-term mitigation (PrivateNet auth failures)

Thanks for joining the 13:00 PDT bridge. Summary and immediate remediation performed: 

Timeline (UTC-7):
- 08:45 — Control-plane rolling upgrade initiated in region, started rotating control-plane pods for groups A/B.
- 08:50 — First customer-reported 401/502 occurrences; token validation failures observed in auth subsystem.
- 09:01 — Targeted rollback of the most-recently rotated control-plane cohort completed; error volume reduced but short spikes continued.
- 09:30–12:30 — Engineering investigation (auth trace correlation, KMS token checks).
- 14:45 — Hotfix deployed (v1.2.3-hotfix) that changes auth-cache invalidation ordering to ensure token validators see the new signing key before cache eviction.
- 15:00 — Monitoring shows successful stabilization; no new Helix Health-authenticated requests failing.

Root cause hypothesis (short):
A change in the control-plane upgrade ordering introduced a small race where token-signing key rotation could occur and trigger cache eviction before all token validators had visibility of the new key. That window produced spurious token validation failures for a subset of requests.

Actions taken:
- Immediate rollback of the latest cohort to reduce exposure.
- Hotfix (1.2.3-hotfix) deployed to restore safe ordering for cache invalidation.
- Added additional health checks and delay window in the rolling upgrade controller to prevent key-cooldown races.
- Created SUP ticket SUP-9876 to track follow-on work and to instrument additional correlation ids for future incidents.

Next steps:
- We’ll schedule a remediation/patch window to backport the fix and run a controlled rollout for your cluster (proposed: Tue 2028-06-26 10:00 PDT).
- Deliver a written postmortem tomorrow (we expect to send by 11:30 PDT 2028-06-27).
- We are offering a goodwill SLA credit for the time within the impact window; I will follow up with billing and your account rep.

Attachments: controlplane-traces-0625.json (subset of auth traces), postmortem-draft-0627.pdf (internal draft)

If you need logs or additional telemetry right now I can surface those. Appreciate the patience and the quick collaboration on the bridge.

Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwoodinference.com>

Date: Thu, 27 Jun 2028 11:30:00 -0700
Subject: Post-incident summary: PrivateNet authentication failures (2028-06-25) — RCA and next steps

Hello Sofia —

Thanks again for your time during the bridge on 6/25. Below is our formal post-incident summary and remediation plan. Please let me know if you’d like a walkthrough.

Impact:
- Customers affected: Helix Health private deployment (hlx-prod-5)
- Impact window: 2028-06-25 08:45–09:05 PDT (primary), with isolated retries until ~09:30 PDT.
- Observable effects: short-lived 401/502 responses for management-plane calls and failed webhook deliveries.

Root cause (detailed):
- A control-plane upgrade introduced a change in cache eviction ordering related to token-signing key rotation. During the rolling upgrade, cache eviction for some validators occurred before the new signing key was visible to all token validators, resulting in a transient validation window where newly issued tokens could not be verified.

Remediation performed: 
- Rolled back the latest upgraded cohort immediately upon detection to reduce error volume.
- Deployed a hotfix (v1.2.3-hotfix) that enforces ordered key propagation and adds a short verification gating step before cache eviction.
- Added a 30s cooldown and extra health-check gating to the rolling upgrade controller to avoid ordering races in future upgrades.
- Instrumented additional correlation ids in token validation flow for faster root cause tracing.

Preventative actions and timeline:
- 2028-06-25 (same day): rollback + hotfix deployed; stabilization confirmed.
- 2028-06-26: Planned controlled backport and verification rollout for hlx-prod-5 (completed without incident).
- 2028-06-27: Finalized postmortem and updated operator runbooks; added automated pre-upgrade verification step to CI/CD.

Customer support and remediation:
- We will issue a goodwill SLA credit covering the primary impact window; your account rep will follow up with the exact credit calculation and paperwork.
- Offer: optional deeper telemetry export for Helix Health’s internal SREs; we can share raw auth traces on request.

Attachments: postmortem-draft-0627.pdf (finalized), controlplane-logs-0625.tar.gz (full logs)

Apologies again for the disruption. If you’d like a 1:1 review or to go over the technical details with our engineering leads, we can set that up this week.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Senior Customer Reliability Manager
Redwood Inference
